recipes.name: FRENCH ONION SOUP
ingredients: 6 cups high quality beef stock (or amped up store bought stock, see below)
day old French baguette, for topping
For the Amped Up Store Bought Stock
instructions: For the Soup

Begin by preparing your onions. Peel them and then cut in half from pole to pole - through the root and stem. Remove the tough root part by cutting it away with your knife. Then thinly slice them pole to pole - like cutting with the grain of the onion. This gives the slices more structural integrity so that they stand up to the slow cooking method. - 3 lbs Spanish onions
Repeat this process with the rest of the onions. - 3 lbs Spanish onions
Next prepare your stock. Ideally you would use homemade beef stock, but you can also “soup” up a store bought version. - 6 cups high quality beef stock (or amped up store bought stock see below)
For the Amped Up Stock

Add your beef broth to a stock pot and bring to a simmer. Add aromatics like parsley, sliced carrots, thyme sprigs, garlic, bay leaves, peppercorns, cloves, and parmesan rind. Let it simmer for 1 hour. - 6 cups high quality beef stock (or amped up store bought stock see below) - 1 bunch parsley - 3 large carrots sliced - thyme sprigs - 3 garlic cloves halved - 2 bay leaves - sprinkle of peppercorns - 2 cloves optional - parmesan cheese rind
For the Soup
In a large Dutch oven drizzle olive oil and let heat up for one minute. Dump in the sliced onions. It will look like way too many, but just trust me. - 3 tbsp olive oil - 3 lbs Spanish onions
Slowly caramelize the onions over medium heat. Keep them moving constantly, and scrape down the sides of the pot. - 3 lbs Spanish onions
The onions are done when they are soft, jammy, and caramelized with a lot of fond on the bottom of the pot. - 3 lbs Spanish onions
Add flour to the onions and cook for 1-2 minutes. - 2 tbsp flour - 3 lbs Spanish onions
Deglaze the pot with dry sherry and cook, scraping up fond from the bottom of the pot. - 1 cup dry sherry
Once the alcohol is cooked off, add the beef broth. Make sure to strain it first if you added aromatics. - 6 cups high quality beef stock (or amped up store bought stock see below)
Let the whole thing simmer for 5-10 minutes to let the flavors get to know each other.
Optional: add umami boosters. I like to add a splash of fish sauce and soy sauce to richen the flavors. - fish sauce optional - soy sauce optional

Cut thick slices of day-old french baguette. Put them on a baking sheet. Drizzle with olive oil and top with salt and pepper. - day old French baguette for topping - 3 tbsp olive oil - kosher salt to taste - black pepper to taste
Toast bread in a 400°F oven for 5 minutes. - day old French baguette for topping
Slice a clove of garlic in half and rub down each piece of bread with the garlic. - 1 garlic cloves halved - day old French baguette for topping
Check the soup for salt and pepper and season as necessary. - kosher salt to taste - black pepper to taste
Ladle soup into broiler-safe cups. Top with sliced baguette and shredded cheese. - day old French baguette for topping - Gruyere cheese shredded, for topping
Put the bowls onto a baking sheet and put into an oven preheated to broil. Broil at your broiler’s high setting or at 500°F for 3-5 minutes until golden brown.
Garnish with chives and serve and enjoy! - chopped chives for garnish
